description: The pie chart represents the distribution of various news sources, comparing their relative proportions. The chart is divided into 16 slices, each representing a different news source. The slices are labeled with the name of the news source and are colored differently, although some colors are similar and not easily distinguishable. The proportions of the slices are as follows: Breitbart (blue, 14%), Other (dark grey, 13%), PoliticusUSA (pink, 8%), The Daily Caller (red, 8%), Drudge Report (green, 8%), The Huffington Post (brown, 7%), NPR (light blue, 7%), Vox (purple, 6%), The Guardian (pink, 5%), BBC (light brown, 5%), RT (dark blue, 3%), Daily Kos (yellow, 3%), National Review (light green, 3%), Daily Mail (orange, 3%), Fox News (red, 3%), and CNN (light blue, 3%). The chart does not include a legend, but the labels are placed outside the corresponding slices. The slices are arranged in a seemingly unordered manner, with no apparent visual emphasis on any particular slice.
